summary: Array: binds to a shared client-side array by id — read its items and count, seed its contents, and react to changes made anywhere.
description: Client-side arrays live in a global registry keyed by id: every node that names the same id — this node, Insert/Remove/Clear Array nodes, other components — reads and mutates the same underlying array. Collection2 binds to the array named on `collectionId` (Id) and exposes it on `items` (the live array), plus `count`, `firstItemId` and `id`. Whenever the array's contents change — from any node or code, anywhere in the app — `changed` fires and `count`/`firstItemId` update. Connecting an array to the `items` input copies that source array's contents into this array, and keeps re-copying while the source changes. If `fetch` (signal) is connected the node defers: a new `collectionId` only takes effect when `fetch` fires (then `fetched` fires), and automatic `changed` events are suppressed.
whenToUse: Local list state shared across components without any wiring between them: give every interested node the same Array Id. For server data use DbCollection2 (Query Records); for a single object use Model2 (Object); to mutate the array use Insert/Remove/Clear Array nodes rather than manipulating `items` in code.

ports.collectionId: Value input: the shared array's id. Every node using the same id operates on the same array.
ports.items: As input (value): copies the connected source array's contents into this array, tracking later source changes. As output (value): the shared array itself — feed a Repeater's `items`.
ports.fetch: Signal input; when connected, id changes are deferred until this fires, and the automatic `changed` output is suppressed — use for explicit control over when the node (re)binds.
ports.changed: Signal; fires after the array's contents change from anywhere in the app (suppressed while `fetch` is connected).
ports.fetched: Signal; fires after an explicit `fetch` has re-bound the array.
ports.done: Signal; the outcome of a Fetch. It always accompanies `fetched` on this node, because Fetch is the only path that announces one — the two come apart on its twins Object and Variable, where a name change announces `fetched` with no invocation behind it.
ports.completed: Signal; fires after every Fetch whatever the outcome — wire it to carry on regardless. This node has no Failure, because binding an array cannot fail.
ports.firstItemId: String value: the id of the array's first object, or empty when the array is empty.

patterns: Same `collectionId` in many components: a list page shows the array while a form elsewhere inserts into it — no connections needed between them.
`items` → For Each `items`: the canonical local list.
Feed `collectionId` from Create New Array `id` to bind to a dynamically created array.
antiPatterns: Using it for cloud data — it is purely client-side, nothing is persisted; use DbCollection2 (Query Records) instead.
